commit_message:
Bug 1999464 - Don't nuke CCWs to the debugger object r=jandem

This is an alternative to the fix in bug 1995637 and removes that change.

The debugger mostly uses its own wrappers for cross compartment pointers
between debugger and debuggee globals. These are not in the CCW map and so are
not nuked by NukeCrossCompartmentWrappers. This pointer from a Breakpoint to
its owning debugger however is a normal CCW that is in the map and so can be
affected by that operation.

The change makes it so we skip nuking CCWs to the main debugger object. This
could affect other uses of this CCW but these are not accessible from content
JS so I don't think this is a problem.

It's important not to break the link between breakpoints and their debuggers
because they are present in two linked lists which are in different realms. To
clean up properly the link needs to be intact.

This change is also covered by the original test in bug 1995637.

Differential Revision: https://phabricator.services.mozilla.com/D273012

fix_commit.author: Jon Coppeard

findings.title: Use-after-free from asymmetric nuke/create rules for debugger CCWs
findings.message: NukeCrossCompartmentWrappers() was changed so that it skips nuking existing cross-compartment wrappers (CCWs) that point at a Debugger instance object (used to link Breakpoints back to their owning Debugger across realms). However, the companion function js::AllowNewWrapper(), which governs whether a *new* CCW may be created into a compartment/realm that has already had NukeCrossCompartmentWrappers() called on it (via the nukedOutgoingWrappers / nukedIncomingWrappers flags), was left unmodified. This created an inconsistency: an existing CCW to a Debugger instance survives nuking and stays live and usable, but if code subsequently needs to create a *new* CCW to that same (already-nuked) debugger realm -- e.g. while wrapping a fresh reference to the debugger object during debugger operations such as accessing an environment/variable after nukeAllCCWs() -- AllowNewWrapper() unconditionally refuses, since it has no exception for DebuggerInstanceObject. Compartment::wrap() then falls back to producing a dead-object-proxy substitute in a situation where its invariants assume a live wrapper is obtainable (because a live debugger CCW already exists elsewhere), corrupting the compartment's wrapper map: the same debugger object ends up simultaneously represented by a live wrapper and treated through paths that expect a dead one. This mismatched/incoherent wrapper state can be exploited to reach and use a JS object after the compartment's outgoing wrappers were logically invalidated, resulting in a use-after-free (CVE-2026-0884), reproduced by jit-test bug-2003588.js and bug-2003809.js (Debugger + nukeAllCCWs()/recomputeWrappers()/gc() sequences).
findings.suggestion: When introducing an exception in NukeCrossCompartmentWrappers() that leaves an object's existing CCW un-nuked, add the matching exception in AllowNewWrapper() so that new wrappers for the same class of objects (DebuggerInstanceObject) can still be created into a target that has already been marked as nuked. Otherwise the nuke/allow-creation policy diverges and Compartment::wrap()'s invariant that a live wrapper is always obtainable for such objects is violated, leading to wrapper-map corruption and use-after-free.

ground_truth.root_cause: An earlier fix (bug 1999464) special-cased NukeCrossCompartmentWrappers() to leave CCWs pointing at DebuggerInstanceObject un-nuked, but the matching AllowNewWrapper() gate (which blocks creation of new CCWs into compartments/realms already marked as nuked) was not given the same exception. This mismatch between 'existing wrapper survives' and 'new wrapper creation is still blocked' violates invariants assumed by Compartment::wrap(), leading to corrupted/incoherent wrapper state and eventually use-after-free.
